newsitem.title: USA: Clinton calls his win a triumph for "vital center".
newsitem.headline: Clinton calls his win a triumph for "vital center".

text.p: President Bill Clinton said on Wednesday his re-election represented a victory for "the vital center" of American politics.

"The American people sort of moved back toward the vital center after Oklahoma City," Clinton told reporters aboard the presidential jet returning him to Washington from Arkansas where he spent election night. He referred to the 1995 bombing of a federal building in Oklahoma City, attributed by law enforcement officials to anti-government extremists.
"I think a lot of the bitter, bitter rhetoric (after the bombing) ... broke a spell in the country as people began searching for our common ground again," Clinton said.

He defeated Republican Bob Dole handily in electoral votes on Tuesday but, according to the latest official returns, fell just short of the popular vote majority he had sought. He said he might have added a percentage point or to to his support if he had not spent much time near the end campaigning in small states for Democratic congressional candidates.

Officials said turnout was the lowest ever for a U.S. presidential election and Clinton blamed that on the Republicans, saying the "were doing everything they could to drive the turnout down. They did a good job."

The voters also decided to keep Congress under the control of a Republican majority in both houses, but the president said he was nonetheless "elated" at the overall results and the support he got all across the land.
